videos.title: All Jokers Tier List (Commons)
videos.why: Ranks all 61 commons: early flat +Mult over chips, discards and hands as money, consistency over variance, money-joker ordering

videos.title: All Jokers Tier List (Uncommons)
videos.why: Ranks uncommons: xMult priority, fragility to bosses, skip cost (Throwback), deck-size limits, money/value generators

videos.title: All Jokers Tier List (Rares and Legendaries)
videos.why: Ranks rares/legendaries: copy jokers, hand-xMult rares, bosses-halve-score model; partly on fun/design

claims.statement: Common flat-scoring jokers (+Mult/+Chips hand-type jokers, Jimbo, sinful jokers, chips jokers) and common money jokers are bought in antes 1-2 to survive; treat every common as effectively perishable and plan to sell it for an uncommon/xMult scorer or better Planet levels later.

conditions.build_state: buying commons early; selling them from ~ante 3 when a better scorer is offered

quotes.text: you're not taking these things in anti 4 you're not taking these things in anti 6 you're taking these things in the first two an and then that's it and then you sell them to anties later
every common Joker that you pick up is perishable if you pick up a money generating Joker it's perishable you will reach a point in the game where you have to sell it to score more points
at the time that you get these Commons they do the thing that they need you to do they do survival for you

claims.knob: joker value for common flat-scoring jokers: full in antes 1-2, decaying from ante 3 (e.g. x0.6 by ante 4); when slots are full and an uncommon/rare scorer or xMult is offered, sell the weakest common
claims.notes: He says this most directly about the hand-type +Mult commons; the 'perishable' remark covers money commons too.

claims.statement: For the hand-type commons, every +Mult version beats every +Chips version. Early you want the +Mult; later you want neither. Chips jokers fall off because Planet levels give mostly chips (e.g. +20 to +30 chips per +1 to +2 Mult).

quotes.text: early on early on I'd rather have the plus mol later on I'd rather not have any of these so like that's kind of the tension here
I think all of the chips are going to be worse than all of the Mt
the ratio is much higher chips leaning on the planet cards and so all of these chips generators fall off later on

claims.knob: value(+Chips hand joker: Sly/Wily/Clever/Devious/Crafty) < value(matching +Mult joker), e.g. x0.6; both decay toward 0 after ante 3-4

claims.statement: Rank the hand-type +Mult commons by ease of the hand times payoff: Droll (Flush +10) > Mad (Two Pair +10) > Crazy (Straight +12) > Jolly (Pair +8, 'mid') > Jimbo (+4, $2, 'mid') > Zany (Three of a Kind +12, too hard to make). Use the same order for the +Chips versions (Crafty middle, Sly 'basically free but only 50 chips', Wily lowest).

quotes.text: probably for me the best of these set is going to be droll and I think droll what I like about droll is it's really easy to make flushes
I actually prefer mad better because of how easy it is to make two pair for the plus 10 and probably the worst of these I actually put Jimbo above zany
I would rank them in probably the same order as far as like you know the what is the difficulty of making the hand versus like you know what is the reward that you get

claims.knob: hand-type joker value table: Droll 1.0, Mad 0.95, Crazy 0.9, Jolly 0.8, Joker 0.7, Zany 0.6 (relative); chips versions same order scaled down

claims.statement: Early, +Mult that works on any hand (Half Joker +20 when playing <=3 cards, Abstract, Mystic Summit +15, Gros Michel +15, Smiley Face, Even Steven, the suit 'sinful' jokers) is worth more than hand-type +Mult. The sinful jokers rank above hand-type jokers because a 3-card partial flush already gives +9.

quotes.text: I think the solid unrestricted sources of Plus Mt are insane early game very stable
plus 15 to any hand that you play any garbage that you play plus 15 which is Big
you don't have to play the full flush you could just play a straight that has only three cards and it would still be nine mol

roffle.note: Roffle skips cheap early flat scoring at White stake and banks the money; BU (no stake given) calls unrestricted +Mult 'insane early game' and buys these commons in antes 1-2.

claims.knob: early-game value multiplier for any-hand +Mult jokers vs hand-type +Mult jokers (e.g. x1.3); Half Joker / Abstract / sinful / Smiley / Even Steven in the top common group
claims.notes: Relevant to the White-stake target: BU gives no stake restriction here.

claims.statement: Expect to hold about 4 jokers by the end of ante 2 (said while valuing Abstract, which starts around +12 and reaches ~+15).

quotes.text: you get up to 4 four Jokers within the first two anties and so I think abstract it's easy smash for me

claims.knob: target >= 4 filled joker slots by the end of ante 2 (fill with cheap scoring/money jokers)
claims.notes: Said once in passing; the 4 is his estimate of typical joker count, read here as a target (implied).

claims.statement: A flat chips source (about +100 chips from Odd Todd, Ice Cream, Runner, Blue Joker) makes any hand score about the same in the short term. Then play throwaway High Card or Pair and spend discards digging for Gold cards and Purple/Blue Seals instead of chasing a hand. This is why he puts Odd Todd above Even Steven.

quotes.text: if you have like plus 100 chips then it doesn't matter if you play a flush it doesn't matter if you play a pair they're both going to score relatively you know about the same amount of points
you can use your discards for Value um and you don't have to worry about what hand that you're trying to make

claims.knob: if flat joker chips >= ~100: hand chooser ignores hand-type preference (play cheapest winning hand) and discards target Gold/sealed cards

claims.statement: Jokers that ask you not to discard (Banner, Green Joker, Delayed Gratification, Ramen, and in effect Blue Joker) lose value, because discards dig for Gold cards and Purple Seals. With even one Purple Seal or Gold card in the deck, sell Delayed Gratification and don't buy Banner.

conditions.build_state: deck has >= 1 Purple Seal or Gold card

quotes.text: the main thing that I use discarding for is for digging for gold cards which then give you value digging for purple seals which then give you value
having just one purple seal in your deck just one that's enough for you to sell your gratification that's enough for you to not buy Banner yeah same even just a gold card
not being able to use your discards discards are a lot of value discards allow you to get gold cards discards allow you to get purple seals

claims.knob: if deck has >= 1 Purple Seal or Gold card: Delayed Gratification gets high sell priority, Banner/Green Joker/Ramen value x0.5
claims.notes: The 'one purple seal' line is a chatter's point that he reads aloud and endorses ('yeah same even just a gold card'). Late in the commons video he moved Green Joker up a little (to just behind Runner), mentioning Gold-stake players who rate it.

claims.statement: Count each extra hand a joker makes you spend as about $1 lost (unused hands pay $1 each). Dusk (last hand only), Loyalty Card + Burglar (six hands a round), DNA (costs a hand) and Square Joker (four 4-card hands for +16) are all marked down.

quotes.text: dust gives you the re-triggers but it's only on your last hand which is expensive you got to use up your hands your hands are money
why are you spending six hands every round when you could could just be spending three hands or something like that
Square cost me $4 per round if I'm using the runner I'm playing one straight every round anyway it doesn't cost me extra

roffle.note: Roffle: Loyalty Card with six hands a round is a real xMult; BU: six hands a round is too expensive even at its best.

claims.knob: joker value -= $1 x (expected extra hands per round the joker requires); Dusk/Loyalty/DNA/Square penalised

claims.statement: Prefer predictable output to random output with the same average. Misprint (average ~+12, like Abstract) is a pass: when you can make only one scoring hand, a low roll ends the run, and fixed output lets you plan throwaway hands. Bloodstone is the same: it needs three x1.5 procs to beat Acrobat's x3.

quotes.text: if you only have the ability to make one scoring hand getting the low roll can be run ending
I like I like being able to know exactly what's going to happen
it's just not as consistent as you know even like acrobat times three it takes three 1.5s

claims.knob: value random-output jokers (Misprint, Bloodstone, Space Joker, Rough Gem, 8 Ball) at a low percentile of their output (e.g. 25th) rather than the mean, especially early

claims.statement: Once one hand is enough to win the round, play the other hands as throwaways for To-Do List or Rebate money, Purple Seals, Gold cards or levels, and discard more freely. A stable score lets you win with fewer hands and get more value each round.

conditions.build_state: one hand already beats the blind

quotes.text: if you know that I can win every round in just one hand I know that I don't need two flushes I know that I only need one flush then you can be a little bit more liberal with your discarding
often times what I'm looking for is I actually don't want to score points I actually just want to throw away hands for you know to-do list money or rebate money

claims.knob: if projected best hand >= remaining blind chips: spend earlier hands/discards on value actions (To-Do List hand, Rebate rank, sealed/Gold cards), play the winning hand last

claims.statement: Early spending that costs interest can beat interest if it lets you play greedier, e.g. buying more with Credit Card. Otherwise save by buying nothing until you have $25 in the bank (the interest cap).

quotes.text: a early expense in the beginning you know spending down even though it costs you interest can be worth it long term can be better than interest sometimes because it unlocks your ability to play more greedy
normally when you're trying to save money for interest you like okay I just don't buy anything until I have $25 in the bank

claims.knob: antes 1-2: spend on scoring/money jokers even below $25; afterwards a 'saving' state buys nothing until money >= $25
claims.notes: Elsewhere (Bull) he says 'typically I roll a bunch' instead of saving money, so in practice he rerolls more than this rule suggests.

claims.statement: Credit Card: use the debt in one burst. Buy everything in one or two shops, sell the card, then buy nothing until you are out of debt. You rarely find two jokers you want in the same shop, so buying a little each shop is usually better, and he ranks it low (below 8 Ball). Its main use is getting off the ground on Black Deck or Gold stake.

quotes.text: I think like the ideal scenario is you get the credit card you buy everything in one shop where you buy everything in the next shop and then you get rid of it
it's rare for you to find two jokers that you want to buy from the same shop right usually it's a couple rounds before before you find the next Joker that you actually care about
if you're playing on the gold Stak sometimes you just need to get off the ground

roffle.note: Agrees that the debt is for an early burst, but BU ranks the card itself low (behind 8 Ball).

claims.knob: Credit Card joker value low (below 8 Ball); if owned: allow negative money for at most 2 shops, then sell it and freeze purchases until money >= 0
claims.notes: Self-contradiction: at first he called Credit Card a 'gentle smash', better than the hand-type +Mult jokers early, then after a chat challenge moved it behind 8 Ball.

claims.statement: In the first couple of rounds buy a scoring joker before Golden Joker. It costs $6 plus the interest lost and pays $4 a round, so it has to be held several rounds to pay off. He ranks it near the worst money joker, next to Delayed Gratification.

quotes.text: golden Joker cost six you know it cost you twice as much and you get back some of that money
early on I think you know you need some kind of scoring Joker to help you survive the the first couple rounds here

roffle.note: Roffle buys money jokers in antes 1-2 even over a small scoring gain; BU wants a scoring joker first and rates Golden Joker low.

claims.knob: ante 1 with no scoring joker: Golden Joker value below any +Mult common; Golden Joker ~= Delayed Gratification in money-joker table

claims.statement: Money jokers, as he ranks them. Commons: Mail-In Rebate is overtuned (top). Business Card is mid: above Delayed Gratification, below Chaos the Clown. Faceless sits above Gratification. To-Do List is about Business Card but swingier. Golden Joker is about Gratification (low). Reserved Parking and Golden Ticket are passes: Parking nets about $2.5 a round at best after paying a hand ($1), and Ticket earns only $1 more per Gold card played than holding it. Uncommons: Bull and Bootstraps 'off the charts'; Gift Card and Rocket smash; Turtle Bean smash but 'not top tier money'; Cloud 9 conditional; To the Moon below Cloud 9; Satellite pass (too slow to get going).

quotes.text: rebate is imbalanced the number too big and so like you can't use that as your like point of comparison
seven face cards on average gives you 350 or sorry $3.5 but it cost you a dollar so you get 2.5
ticket is one additional dollar one additional dollar right like it gives you $4 per Gold Card played but like if you keep the gold card in your hand it's $3

roffle.note: Roffle lists Reserved Parking, Golden Ticket and Credit Card as early money jokers to take; BU passes on Parking and Ticket and rates Credit Card low.

claims.knob: money-joker value table: Rebate > Clown >= Business Card ~ To-Do > Faceless > Gratification ~ Golden Joker > Golden Ticket, Reserved Parking (pass); uncommon: Bull ~ Bootstraps > Gift Card ~ Rocket > Turtle Bean > Cloud 9 > To the Moon > Satellite
claims.notes: Chaos the Clown was first rated 'easily better than Golden Joker' (~$7/round if you reroll 3x/shop) and then argued down because you need money to reroll, and late in the game the slot is needed for scoring. 'Money's just busted' is his general stance.

claims.statement: Skipping a blind costs that shop and its booster packs, a huge opportunity cost, so he generally doesn't take skip tags. More than about 3 skips in a run goes badly. Throwback is a trap: in three shops you will find an uncommon better than it.

quotes.text: I think skipping booster packs is expensive it's a huge opportunity cost so like you don't skip you don't take skip tags you don't skip rounds you don't take skip tags because you
if you're skipping more than three times probably you're going to have a bad time
if you just shop three times you're going to find an uncommon Joker that's better than throwback

claims.knob: skip a blind at most ~3 times per run, and only when the tag clearly beats the shop + packs lost; Throwback / Diet Cola valued low
claims.notes: Roffle states this only for Gold stake; BU applies it generally. The Diet Cola point: even a doubled skip tag may not be worth the slot.

claims.statement: In Standard packs take the sealed cards (Purple, Blue; the Blue Seal buff makes Blue worth taking now). With no seals, take nothing. He treats Standard packs as high variance.

quotes.text: I think with the buff to the Blue Seal now it's worth it to take Blue Seals from the stand standard packs
standard packs kind of high variants if you get the seals they're good if you don't get the seals you don't take them
from the standard packs you're actually picking up purple seals you're picking up Blue Seals

claims.knob: Standard pack pick: take a card with Purple/Blue (also Gold/Red) Seal; if none, skip the pick (avoid deck bloat)
claims.notes: He mentions a recent Blue Seal buff (the 1.0.1-era change).

claims.statement: Slow +Mult scalers (Ride the Bus at $6, Green Joker, Supernova, Red Card) are weak. By the time they are big you should already be doing something else. Early you need immediate flat +Mult (Half Joker) to carry you while you build economy and the deck.

quotes.text: if you invest a lot into it by the time it becomes big by the time it becomes useful you're already at a point in the game where you should just be doing something else
you need Habs early on to carry you while you're still building up your economy while you're still you know doing the deck building

claims.knob: antes 1-2: value slow +Mult scalers (Bus, Green, Supernova, Red Card) by expected Mult at ante 3, below same-cost flat +Mult jokers
claims.notes: Exception: the reroll-scaling +Mult he calls 'JJ' (likely Flash Card) 'grows so fast' even when picked up later.

claims.statement: With Runner, play one Straight a round for about 6 rounds (or one every other round for about 12), then play Pairs, Flushes or anything else; the banked chips apply to every hand. Runner is a hedge against not finding Saturns, and once Saturns arrive it goes obsolete.

quotes.text: you can play one straight every round for maybe six rounds or you know one straight every other round for like 12 rounds and then just play pears after that just play flushes after that play anything else
the runner gives you a hedge against not getting Saturn cards

claims.knob: with Runner: play a Straight once per round when available (even as a throwaway) until Runner chips >= ~90, then play the best hand

claims.statement: Square Joker is expelled: it takes four 4-card hands to gain what one Straight gives Runner, and each extra hand costs $1. Constellation 'can smash with the best of them'.

quotes.text: Square can get out of my class I don't want to see you on campus ever again
Square takes four hands in order to get the same plus 15 that the runner does
constellation can smash with the best of them

roffle.note: Roffle prefers Square Joker over Constellation early; BU expels Square and rates Constellation among the best uncommons (he does not discuss timing).

claims.knob: Square Joker value ~0 (never buy); Constellation high among uncommons

claims.statement: A High Card plan needs a +Mult scaler (Ride the Bus, Supernova, Green Joker) and a chips source. Without the chips source, Green Joker is trash.

quotes.text: they're not the only thing that you need to make a high card run work you also need a source of chips like you need both and so if you don't get the source of chips then your green Joker is trash

claims.knob: buy Bus/Green/Supernova for High Card only if a chips source (Stuntman, Ice Cream, Odd Todd, Stone/Bull/Castle...) is already owned

claims.statement: Most of the time play five cards per hand, so Splash does nothing and he almost never takes it. Splash only helps when the build is failing.

quotes.text: almost never take it cuz like most of the time what you should be doing you should be playing Five cards and if you're playing Five cards Splash doesn't do anything

claims.knob: hand play: pad played hands to 5 cards with the lowest-value cards (cycle the hand) unless a joker rewards <= 4 cards (Half Joker, Square); Splash value ~0

claims.statement: Among uncommons you are mostly looking for xMult. Unconditional xMult that works with any hand (Steel Joker, Acrobat, Card Sharp, Blackboard, Seeing Double) beats retrigger jokers (Hack, Dusk, Sock and Buskin) and conditional or random xMult (Idol, Bloodstone, Throwback).

quotes.text: I think most of the time what you're looking for you want the the sources of X mol
hack is going to be worse than these like generic X mol steel and acrobat no matter what hand you play you get the X molt it's free

claims.knob: uncommon value: unconditional xMult > retrigger/conditional; prefer xMult over more +Mult once 2-3 +Mult sources exist

claims.statement: Model every boss ability as roughly halving your score (e.g. one that blocks your hands means half as many hands). Some bosses do more than halve it: they end the run.

quotes.text: I think of every boss of or yeah, every boss kind of divides your score by two.
Except there's some bosses that don't just give you half your score. Some bosses just end you.

claims.knob: boss readiness: require projected round score >= 2x boss chip requirement (or apply x0.5 to projected score) before the boss; if a boss counters the core plan, buy an answer or reroll the boss
claims.notes: Said while explaining why Chicot is a 'free x2'.

claims.statement: Judge the build by whether it beats the next ante's Small Blind without boss-only help. That Small Blind is about the size of the boss you just beat, so boosts that only fire on the boss (Loyalty Card timed to bosses, a Campfire built up for the boss) leave a gap.

quotes.text: now I have to do the small blind which is the same size as the boss but I have to do it without the help of the loyalty card

claims.knob: build-strength metric = sustainable per-round score vs next ante Small Blind (~ current boss size); don't count one-shot/boss-timed boosts

claims.statement: Matador pays off against only about a third of bosses, and it baits you into greed. He'd still take it quietly.

quotes.text: I think if I go through the list of bosses I think it works a third of the time
really what it is the Matador is not baiting the boss the banador is baiting me baiting me into being greedy

claims.knob: Matador value = $8 x P(next boss triggers on your hand) with P~0.33 by default; check the actual upcoming boss

claims.statement: Card Sharp's x3 is easy to get on most hands, but The Eye, The Mouth and The Needle shut it off, so it's fragile.

conditions.build_state: Card Sharp is a main xMult

quotes.text: Card sharp loses to specific bosses like the eye and the mouth one of them is like you can't repeat hand types
oh yeah card sharp also loses to the needle yeah I think it's a little bit fragile

claims.knob: Card Sharp value x0.8; if Card Sharp is the main xMult and the boss is Eye/Mouth/Needle, reroll the boss (Director's Cut) or buy an answer

claims.statement: Face-card payoff jokers carry boss risk: bosses that flip face cards face-down or debuff them (The Plant) can end a face build. He passes on Pareidolia for this, and Triboulet 'baits' you into going all-in on face cards.

quotes.text: it does have this big drawback of the bosses that mess with your face cards like all your face cards face down or you know disabling all your face cards
get the face card debuff boss and then it's over. Yeah, the plant.

claims.knob: Pareidolia value low; in face builds keep non-face scoring backup and treat The Plant as must-answer (reroll/plan)

claims.statement: Don't bloat the deck. After about 6 added cards he doesn't want a seventh or to go above 60 cards (Hologram). DNA is a pass because it adds cards and costs a hand: Four of a Kind needs only four copies. Marble Joker is 'classic deck bloat'.

quotes.text: once you've added like six cards to your deck I don't know if I want to add a seventh card to my deck
DNA adds a card to my deck. Even if it's my best card. I I've said this before. If you want to play four of a kind, you only need four to play four of a kind.

claims.knob: cap additions at ~start size + 6 (about 58-60 cards) unless a joker rewards size (Hologram/Erosion inverse); DNA/Marble value low

claims.statement: Value generators: Trading Card (card removal plus money) does more than Constellation. Hallucination is about as good as Cartomancer (about 1 Tarot a round) and both are top. Superposition (often under 1 a round off Abandoned Deck) and 8 Ball (~1 a round only with lots of 8s) are lower. Vagabond's random Tarots are worse than Trading Card's removal and money.

quotes.text: constellation doesn't do as much as trading card trading card gives you two benefits you get the card removal and you get the money
Hallucination is as good or perhaps sometimes better than cartomancer and cardom mancer is an uncommon that cost you six bucks
Why would I want random tarot cards when I can just get the best just card removal and money.

claims.knob: value table: Trading Card > Constellation; Hallucination ~ Cartomancer (top commons/uncommon generators) > Superposition (deck-dependent: ~1.6/round on Abandoned, ~0.7 else) > 8 Ball
claims.notes: The Superposition per-round figures come from a chatter he reads aloud, after which he demoted it.

claims.statement: Gift Card goes the whole run and you never sell it. It turns every later Temperance into a big payout (up to $50, often several in one ante), and it also raises the sell value of held consumables.

quotes.text: gift card you never sell it gift card goes all the way every time
it enables all of future Temperance cards which are pretty easy to get multiple Temperance cards in the same ante

claims.knob: Gift Card: never sell; Temperance value = min($50, total joker sell value) once Gift Card is owned

claims.statement: With the reroll-scaling +Mult joker he calls 'JJ' (most likely Flash Card) you can spend 5-10 rerolls in one shop. It grows so fast that its flat +Mult beats Card Sharp's x3 and you stop needing Glass cards or Planets.

quotes.text: what's cool about JJ is you can spend like f 5 to 10 rerolls in the same shop
JJ gets big enough that you don't need glass cards you don't need Planet cards if JJ gets big enough

claims.knob: if Flash Card owned: raise per-shop reroll budget to 5-10 when money allows (still keep the interest floor per econ.reroll-only-from-surplus)
claims.notes: The joker name is inferred: the captions say 'JJ', but the description (scales from rerolls, '5 to 10 rerolls in the same shop', speedrun money) fits Flash Card. He also says he typically 'rolls a bunch' rather than saving (Bull section).

claims.statement: Decaying jokers are fine for the few rounds you need them. Popcorn gives +20, +16, +12 over three rounds. Ice Cream starts at +100 chips and 'saves runs'. Gros Michel is now 1 in 6 to die (was 1 in 4) but still can't be relied on; the chance at Cavendish is what makes it worth buying.

quotes.text: popcorn gives me 20 16 and 12 that's it I only need it for three rounds
Michelle now one and six chance instead of one and four chance
the thing that like takes it over the top for me is you have the chance of getting Cavendish

claims.knob: decaying jokers valued by sum of output over next ~3 rounds; Gros Michel value includes P(Cavendish later)
claims.notes: Gros Michel odds: he notes the 1.0.1 change from 1 in 4 to 1 in 6.

claims.statement: Most uncommons are situational: whatever you are doing, many of them are useless to you. When the run needs a specific answer (e.g. Luchador against a killer boss), spend all the money and reroll down to get it.

quotes.text: most uncommons are situational and like most of the time whatever you got going on there's going to be a ton of stuff that you don't want to see
when you do need it you're going to you're going to go out of your way you're going to spend all the money you're going to reroll down you're going to get the Luchador

claims.knob: if the next boss counters the build and an answer joker exists: allow rerolling below the interest floor (down to $0) to find it

claims.statement: Usually don't play Glass cards; save them for emergencies when you need the big hand (playing them risks shattering).

quotes.text: most of the time with the glass cards what you want to do is you don't actually want to play them you want to save them until an emergency situation

claims.knob: hand chooser: leave Glass cards out of the played hand when the hand already beats the remaining blind without them

claims.statement: His default deck plan concentrates one suit. That's why Ancient Joker, which wants a rotating suit, usually arrives too late to fit and is 'in the wrong class'.

quotes.text: most of the time I do want to have all same suits a lot of the time. Like that's just the default state.

claims.knob: suit-converting Tarots (Star/Moon/Sun/World) target the majority suit; Ancient Joker value low

claims.statement: In a normal run (to ante 8), held-in-hand builds are weaker than they look. Mime is 'mid' and worse than Photograph, and Baron+Mime is endless thinking. Baron needs kings actually drawn, plus levels in Three of a Kind/Pair/High Card, which you don't usually level. He still rates Baron highly ('I would smash').

quotes.text: people people are just like endless pilled you know like oh it's it's just Baron and mime every time but like in a real run MIM is mid
Baron is at its best when you level up your three of a kind, your pairs, and your high card, which you're not going to do all the time because it's typically like bad to do that.

claims.knob: Mime value modest (below Photograph); Baron value conditional on Kings in deck (>= 4) and Steel/held cards

claims.statement: Rares: Blueprint 'does everything' (overpowered). Brainstorm is a more restrictive, worse Blueprint. Baseball Card is the top smash but needs a couple of uncommons, which isn't hard to have. Stuntman's +250 chips equals about 15 Jupiter levels on Flush. Campfire very consistently passes x10 and is close to a free x2 if you collect many consumables. Duo/Trio/Order/Tribe/Family are 'mid' among rares: Duo and Trio best, Family worst.

quotes.text: I mean blueprint does all of the thing. It does everything, right?
Stuntman or the the baseball card, you kind of need to have a couple uncommons, though. It's not too hard to have multiple uncommons.
I very consistently get this you know above X10.

claims.knob: rare value table: Blueprint ~ Baseball Card ~ Yorick top; Campfire, Baron, Stuntman, Triboulet high; Brainstorm below Campfire; Duo/Trio > Order > Tribe > Family ('mid'); Driver's License mid; DNA, Ancient, Obelisk, Vagabond low
claims.notes: His rare and legendary rankings mix in fun and design (Obelisk is 'strong' but expelled for not being fun; Vagabond for being a lot of work; Chicot held down for 'making the game boring'), so don't read rows as pure power.

claims.statement: Driver's License is 'mid': 16 enhanced cards within 8 antes is tough (he thinks 12 would be reasonable), so it only fits a deck already heavy with enhancements.

quotes.text: Yeah, you know, in eight anties getting 16 enhanced cards might be kind of tough actually.

claims.knob: Driver's License value conditional on enhanced-card count (e.g. >= 10 enhanced by purchase time)

claims.statement: Fortune Teller is retroactive (it counts Tarots already used this run), so you don't buy it early. It's a later pickup once many Tarots have been used.

quotes.text: fortune teller is retroactive fortune teller obviously you're not going to pick it up early but when you find it later

claims.knob: Fortune Teller value = +1 Mult x tarots used so far; skip in antes 1-2

joker_tiers.when_good: +4 Mult for $2; cheap early filler

scale.verbal_verdicts: For nearly every joker he gives a 'smash or pass' verdict instead of naming the row: smash = he'd take it, pass/no = he wouldn't. Strength of the smash, high to low: 'easy/easiest/top-of-the-line/big-time smash' and 'off the charts' > 'proud smash' > 'smash' > 'smash but not proud / wouldn't tell anybody' > 'gentle/soft smash' > 'conditional smash' > 'mid' > 'pass'/'no'. Most rows are set by dragging on screen and only some are said aloud; `row` is filled only when he names it (or a chatter names it and he accepts).
caveats: Rankings are partly vibes, art and fun ('this is based on Vibes only'): Obelisk is called 'very strong' but expelled for not being fun, Vagabond for being a lot of work, Chicot held down because it 'makes the game boring', and Brainstorm and Midas Mask are discussed partly on art.
Commons are judged relative to commons ('we're talking about commons here'); a common 'easy smash' is not worth an uncommon 'smash'.

Several placements moved after chat donations or arguments (Credit Card, 8 Ball, Clown, Superposition, Red Card, Golden Joker, Green Joker, Erosion, Lucky Cat, Luchador, Brainstorm, Vagabond); the table gives the final stated position where one exists.
The uncommon video opens with 'we're going to cut all that stuff out', so some uncommons (e.g. Four Fingers) were never placed in the captions.
scale.rough_power_reading: Not his words: a rough reading of the verbal verdicts for a value table. easy smash/top ~ S-A, smash ~ B, mid/conditional ~ C, pass ~ D, expelled/wrong class ~ F.
